steps.title: Sterilize and germinate sorghum seeds
steps.instruction: Surface‑sterilize sorghum seeds in 30 % commercial bleach with 0.2 % Tween‑20, agitate 20 min, discard floating seeds, wash five times with sterile water (2 min each), optionally treat fungal contamination with 5 % Captan overnight then wash, place seeds on sterile Petri dishes with two Whatman filter papers moistened with 5 mL sterile water, seal with parafilm and incubate in the dark at 30 °C for the experiment‑specified duration.

steps.title: Sterilize and pre‑condition Striga seeds
steps.instruction: Weigh a small batch of dry Striga seeds on a filter paper, record mass, count seeds under a stereomicroscope to determine seeds / mg (repeat ≥3 times for an average). Wash seeds in 10 % bleach with 0.02 % Tween‑20 for 10 min, discard solution, wash five times with sterile water, then pre‑condition at 30 °C in the dark (duration depends on experiment).

steps.title: Assess Striga germinability
steps.instruction: Sterilize a defined amount of Striga seeds, spread on two sterile filter papers moistened with 5 mL sterile water in a Petri dish, pre‑condition at 30 °C in the dark for 10–14 days, transfer seeds to a new dish with 5 mL of 1 ppm GR24rac, incubate 30 °C dark for 3 days, count total and germinated seeds, calculate germination rate (GR % = Ngs/Nts × 100). Use this rate to compute required germinable seeds per plant with the formula provided, then mix sand with sterile water to ~16 % (v/w) moisture, add calculated Striga seeds, incubate sand–seed mix at 30 °C dark for 10–14 days; prepare a negative‑control sand mix identically without Striga.

steps.title: Air‑dry and gamma‑sterilize soil
steps.instruction: Air‑dry soil at room temperature for 4–7 days, sieve through a 4 mm mesh, then sterilize by gamma irradiation at 8 kGy.

steps.title: Prepare soil plugs and grow sorghum seedlings
steps.instruction: Moisten each soil batch (sterilized and non‑sterilized) with sterile water to 5 % (w/v) moisture. Cut a drainage hole in the bottom of a 50 mL conical tube, wrap tube in aluminum foil (leave hole uncovered). Fill tube with soil, make a 1 mL‑tip hole, place a 3‑day‑old sorghum seedling into the hole, and cover with soil. Grow tubes in a greenhouse or growth chamber at 28 °C day/25 °C night, 11 h light, 450 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, 70 % RH; add 3 mL sterile deionized water to each plug every second day. Grow for 10 days.

steps.title: Prepare cones and plant sorghum with sand‑Striga mix
steps.instruction: Autoclave cones, cover bottom hole with a gauze pad secured by a rubber band. Fill each cone with 350 mL fresh sand, then top up with 350 mL pre‑conditioned sand (with or without Striga seeds, 3 000 germinable seeds per plant as determined in step 3). Make a hole in the cone to receive the 10‑day‑old sorghum seedling with its soil plug, place seedling, cover plug surface with a thin layer of fresh sand. Grow in the same chamber conditions as step 5. Apply 50 mL sterile half‑strength Hoagland solution on days 0, 7, 14 and 50 mL sterile deionized water on days 1, 4, 10, 13, 17.

steps.title: Quantify Striga infection on sorghum roots
steps.instruction: At 14 or 21 days after transfer to cones, gently remove the plant, shake off sand, collect all substrate, swirl roots in a water‑filled tray, dry roots with paper towel, cut root system from shoot, record fresh weight, place roots in a water‑filled transparent tray, examine under a 10× stereomicroscope for attached and penetrated Striga (using Figures 2D‑E as reference). Count de‑attached Striga recovered from substrate, sum penetrated and de‑attached numbers for total penetration, then normalize total Striga count and attachment number by root fresh weight.

steps.title: Collect sorghum root exudates
steps.instruction: Place a 1 L beaker under a cone, pour 300 mL sterile water into the cone, collect 100 mL flow‑through, store refrigerated until use.

steps.title: In‑vitro Striga germination and haustorium assay – seed plating
steps.instruction: Place a sterile glass‑fiber filter paper in a 94 mm polystyrene Petri dish, add 3 mL sterile deionized water, spread sterilized Striga seeds (≈200 per plate) on the wet filter, seal with parafilm, pre‑condition at 30 °C dark for 6–8 days, then dry seeds in a laminar flow hood.

steps.title: In‑vitro assay – seed treatment
steps.instruction: Transfer ~30 pre‑conditioned Striga seeds to each well of a 6‑well plate, add 50–200× diluted root exudate (to achieve ~40–50 % germination) in three technical replicates; for haustorium formation, add undiluted exudate plus 1 ppm GR24rac (first add GR24rac to induce uniform germination). Include positive controls: 1 ppm GR24rac for germination and 100 mM DMBQ for haustorium formation. Incubate plates in the dark at 30 °C for 2 days, then count germinated seeds, haustoria, and total seeds per well. Calculate germination rate (GR % = Ngs/Nts × 100) and haustorium formation rate (HFR % = NHs/Ngs × 100).

steps.title: Prepare bacterial inoculum for haustorium assay (F1)
steps.instruction: Streak bacterial strain from glycerol stock onto 1/10‑strength TSB agar (1.5 % w/v agar), incubate 26 °C dark 24–48 h. Prepare liquid 1/10‑strength TSB broth, autoclave 30 min at 121 °C, inoculate with a single colony, incubate 24 h at 25 °C shaking 200 rpm, measure OD₆₀₀, centrifuge 20 000 rcf 5 min, wash pellet twice with 10 mL sterile 0.9 % NaCl, resuspend to OD₆₀₀ = 0.15 in 0.9 % NaCl.

steps.title: Haustorium formation assay with bacterial filtrates (F2)
steps.instruction: In a 60 mm Petri dish place two sterile glass‑fiber filter papers, add 3 mL sterile water; add four 13 mm filter papers, add sterile water to bring 80–100 Striga seeds per disc, pipette 100 µL of the seed‑water mix onto each 13 mm disc, seal with parafilm, incubate 11 days at 30 °C dark. On day 12 add 100 µL of 1 µM GR24rac (in DMSO) to each disc, reseal and incubate 28 °C 48 h. Simultaneously, inoculate 1 mL liquid TSB broth with a single bacterial colony, incubate 24 h at 25 °C shaking 200 rpm, measure OD₆₀₀, centrifuge 20 000 rcf 5 min, wash cells twice with sterile 0.9 % NaCl, adjust to OD₆₀₀ = 0.15. Mix 18 µL bacterial suspension with 332 µL TSB broth containing 100 µM syringic acid or 50 µM vanillic acid (dissolved in methanol); include a methanol‑only negative control. Incubate 24 h at 25 °C shaking 200 rpm, collect cell‑free filtrate, add 50 µL filtrate to pre‑germinated Striga discs, reseal and incubate 25 °C dark 48 h. Photograph discs under a dissecting microscope.

steps.title: Quantify haustorium formation (F3)
steps.instruction: Open ImageJ, load each disc image, use Plugins → Cell Counter → Initialize. Mark Type 1 for non‑germinated seeds, Type 2 for germinated seeds, Type 3 for seeds with haustorium, save markers, note counts in Excel, calculate HFR as described in step 9.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial inoculum for root phenotype assay (G1)
steps.instruction: Streak strain from glycerol stock onto 1/10‑strength TSB agar (1.5 % w/v), incubate 26 °C dark 24–48 h. Inoculate 5 mL liquid 1/10‑strength TSB with a single colony, incubate 24–48 h at 26 °C shaking 200 rpm. Calculate cells needed: 10⁷ CFU g⁻¹ soil × 50 g sand × number of plants. Compute inoculum volume = required cells ÷ (CFU mL⁻¹ of culture). Harvest required volume by centrifugation 7 000 rcf 20 min, resuspend pellet in sterile half‑strength Hoagland solution (5 mL per plant).

steps.title: Inoculate sorghum seedlings in sand tubes (G2)
steps.instruction: Cut drainage hole in a 50 mL conical tube, wrap in aluminum foil (hole uncovered). Add ~50 g sand, apply 5 mL sterile half‑strength Hoagland solution, make a hole with a 1 mL pipette tip, place a 2‑day‑old sorghum seedling, immediately apply 5 mL bacterial inoculum onto the root, bury seedling and sand, grow in greenhouse/chamber at 28 °C day/25 °C night, 11 h light, 450 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, 70 % RH, and add 5 mL sterile water every second day.

steps.title: Harvest root segments for anatomy (H1)
steps.instruction: Remove plant from tube or cone, tap to release sand, wash root, cut a 1–1.5 cm segment from the region of interest (tip, middle crown, or seminal root). Remove lateral roots, avoid wavy or damaged zones.

steps.title: Embed root in agarose and FAA (H2)
steps.instruction: Prepare 5 % (w/v) agarose in water (autoclave, keep warm). Fill 10 mL glass vials with FAA solution (10 % formalin, 50 % ethanol, 5 % acetic acid). Pipette 5 % liquid agarose into an Eppendorf tube, insert root segment straight, allow agarose to solidify, cut off tube bottom with a hot scalpel, push agar plug out, transfer plug into FAA vial ensuring full coverage.

steps.title: Fix and rehydrate root plugs (H3)
steps.instruction: Place FAA‑submerged vials in a vacuum chamber, vacuum infiltrate 10 min, then leave overnight at room temperature. Remove FAA, add 70 % ethanol, incubate 30 min; replace with 50 % ethanol 30 min, then 30 % ethanol 30 min, then 10 % ethanol 30 min, finally replace with sterile deionized water and store plugs at 4 °C.

steps.title: Section root tissue with vibratome (H4)
steps.instruction: Trim a 0.5–0.75 cm piece from the embedded sample perpendicular to the root axis. Glue the agar plug onto a vibratome specimen disc, fill the buffer tray with ice‑cold water, mount the disc, set knife amplitude = 8, speed = 8, section thickness = 300 µm (adjust if tissue pops out). Discard the first section, collect subsequent sections with a fine brush, examine under 10× stereomicroscope, discard blurry/damaged sections, place good sections in a 12‑well plate with water on ice; prepare 3–4 sections per sample for each staining type.

steps.title: Stain sections for suberin (H5)
steps.instruction: Replace water in the 12‑well plate with 0.01 % Fluorol Yellow (in lactic acid, w/v), incubate 30 min at room temperature in the dark with gentle agitation. Remove solution, wash sections 5 min with deionized water (repeat three times). Add 0.5 % aniline blue (in water, w/v), incubate 30 min at room temperature with agitation, wash 10 min with deionized water (repeat four times). Mount sections on microscopy slides with 50 % glycerol (v/v). Image using a confocal laser scanning microscope (excitation 488 nm), adjust gain manually, save as raw .czi file.

steps.title: Quantify suberin fluorescence (H5‑quant)
steps.instruction: Open ImageJ, load each raw .czi image, use Freehand selection to outline representative endodermal cells, choose Analyze → Measure to record Mean Gray Value, repeat for 3–4 cells, average the values to represent mean fluorescent signal.

steps.title: Stain sections for aerenchyma (H6)
steps.instruction: Replace water in the well plate with 0.1 % toluidine blue (m/v in deionized water), incubate 5 min at room temperature with gentle agitation, remove solution, wash 1 min with deionized water (repeat five times). Image sections with a bright‑field microscope and save as .tiff files.

steps.title: Quantify aerenchyma area (H6‑quant)
steps.instruction: Open ImageJ, load each .tiff image, use Freehand selection to outline each aerenchyma lacuna, record area via Measure, add each measurement to the Results table (use Add Noise to mark recorded areas), then outline the total root cross‑section area (TRA) and record. Save results as a .csv file. Calculate total aerenchyma area (TAA) as the sum of lacuna areas and compute aerenchyma proportion = TAA / TRA (typical value ≈30 % for 4‑week crown roots).

steps.title: Measure root porosity (pycnometer assay)
steps.instruction: Weigh an empty pycnometer filled with water (Pw). Remove plant from tube, tap off sand, wash root, gently dry with paper towel, weigh root (R). Place root into pycnometer, refill with water, weigh (Pr). Vacuum infiltrate the pycnometer with root until no air bubbles remain, shaking intermittently, then weigh the pycnometer with root and water after infiltration (Pv). Calculate root system porosity = (Pv ‑ Pr) / (Pw + R ‑ Pr). Typical mock porosity ≈8.4 % for 10‑day sorghum roots.
